mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D (2GD-FTV) engine replacement typically costs £3,800-£4,500 for a rebuilt unit, £3,200-£3,800 for a reconditioned unit, or £2,500-£3,200 for a used engine. Supply & fit adds approximately £800-£1,200 depending on the specialist and your location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DPF failure in a Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include reduced engine performance, higher fuel consumption, frequent DPF regeneration cycles, a smoky exhaust, and the vehicle entering limp mode. The DPF issue affects the 2GD-FTV engine widely.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical 2016-2018 Hilux 2.4 D-4D is worth £8,000-£15,000. A rebuilt engine at £3,800-£4,500 plus fitting represents 30-50% of the vehicle's value - which is generally worthwhile if the rest of the vehicle is in good condition and you plan to keep it for 2+ years. If the vehicle is worth under £5,000, a used engine or repair may make more sense.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D engine replacement takes 2-5 working days for supply and fit, depending on the specialist's workload and parts availability. Supply-only delivery is usually 1-3 working days nationwide.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D and the 2.8 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.4 D-4D (2GD-FTV) produces 150hp and 400Nm of torque, while the 2.8 D-4D (1GD-FTV) produces 177-204hp and 420-500Nm. The 2.4 is the entry-level diesel option, offering better fuel economy and lower purchase price, while the 2.8 delivers more power for towing and off-road work. Both engines share the same DPF and EGR-related issues.

mainEntity.name: Does the Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D (2GD-FTV) uses a timing chain, not a belt. The chain is designed to last the life of the engine with proper maintenance, though timing chain wear has been reported on higher-mileage units.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D arrived with the eighth-generation Hilux (AN120/AN130) in 2015, replacing the ageing 2.5 D-4D (2KD-FTV) with a cleaner, more efficient 2.4-litre common-rail diesel. The 2GD-FTV engine has remained the entry-level diesel option through two facelifts, with a power bump in 2018.

milestones.description: Power output increased from 150hp to 168hp (125kW) with revised ECU calibration
Facelift model introduced; 2GD-FTV retained with 150hp output, now with manual DPF regeneration switch as standard
Production of 2.4 D-4D variants continues alongside newer powertrains

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 2GD-FTV engine is generally robust, but three issues dominate replacement demand for the Hilux 2.4 D-4D: DPF clogging, EGR valve carbon build-up, and injector wear. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF Clogging - Why the Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D 2GD-FTV Suffers Premature Filter Blockage
problems.rootCause: The DPF fails to regenerate automatically during short journeys or urban driving, causing soot build-up that triggers limp mode, increased fuel consumption, and reduced performance. A class-action lawsuit has been filed over this issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Professional forced regeneration or chemical clean
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix - may recur within 12-24 months
Lasts 60,000+ miles with proper driving habits
Best if combined with other failures or high mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2016-2018 Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D is worth approximately £8,000-£15,000 depending on mileage and condition. With vehicle values in the £8,000-£15,000 band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine typically justifies the premium via warranty and reliability - especially if you're keeping the vehicle for 2+ years.
problems.recommendation: If your Hilux 2.4 D-4D has under 80,000 miles and the DPF is the only issue, a professional clean or replacement is the cost-effective answer. If you're seeing EGR faults or injector problems alongside DPF failure, or if mileage exceeds 120,000, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components often delivers better long-term value than piecemeal repairs.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 2GD-FTV Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D engine prices

problems.h4: EGR Valve Carbon Build-up - Why the Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D 2GD-FTV Loses Power and Economy
problems.rootCause: The EGR valve and cooler become clogged with carbon deposits from recirculated exhaust gas, leading to rough idle, hesitation, increased fuel consumption, and frequent DPF regeneration cycles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve and cooler
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early - may need repeating

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New EGR valve and cooler fitted
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix for the EGR component
Best if combined with DPF or injector failure

problems.recommendation: EGR issues alone rarely justify a full engine replacement. A professional clean or valve replacement is usually sufficient. However, if your Hilux 2.4 D-4D also has DPF problems or injector wear, the combined repair cost often approaches the cost of a rebuilt engine - at which point replacement makes better financial sense.

problems.h4: Injector Wear - Why the Toyota Hilux 2.4 D-4D 2GD-FTV Suffers from Rough Running
problems.rootCause: Denso common-rail injectors wear over time, leading to poor atomisation, rough idle, diesel knock, black smoke, and increased fuel consumption. Poor fuel quality accelerates wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Four new or reconditioned injectors fitted

repairOptions.longevity: Best if combined with DPF or EGR failure

problems.recommendation: Injector wear is a common high-mileage issue. If caught early, reconditioning or replacing the injectors is the sensible route. But if your Hilux 2.4 D-4D is approaching 150,000 miles with multiple issues, a rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty often offers better value than sinking money into an ageing unit.
